metadata.description: A consumable persistent volume: the block or file storage a workload attaches, as distinct from the StorageCluster that provisions it and the device that backs it. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): Kubernetes PVC/CSI and SNIA Swordfish Volume abstract over every consumable volume, so an order for capacity with an access mode is fillable by any provisioner. The provisioner is the provider; a host-local ZFS dataset is a dialect Type beneath it (Volume.ZFS).

access_mode.description: Attachment concurrency: `read_write_once`, `read_only_many`, `read_write_many`, `read_write_once_pod` (the Kubernetes PVC access modes, snake_case).

storage_class.description: Reference to the StorageClass that provisions it; authored by handle, resolved later if the class is not yet defined.

reclaim_policy.description: What happens to the data when the consumer releases the volume: Retain or Delete.

disk_entry.description: The `disks[].name` on the Machine this volume realizes; set exactly when the `realizes_disk` edge is declared. Reconvergence joins on it to fill the machine's `realized_volumes`.

data_source.description: What the volume is filled from when it is created: a VolumeSnapshot (a restore) or another Volume (a clone). Absent means it starts empty.

replica_of.description: The Volume this one is a continuously refreshed copy of.

volume_handle.description: Provider volume handle/id once Realized (CSI volumeHandle / Swordfish Volume Id).

attached.description: Whether the volume is currently attached to a consumer.

accessible_from.description: Where the volume can be attached from, as the provider reports it once Realized (CSI `accessible_topology`, a Kubernetes PV `nodeAffinity`): References to the narrowest scope that reaches it, a Machine.BareMetalHost for host-local storage, a StorageCluster for storage any of its clients can attach, a Location for a site. Placement reads it to put a consumer where its volume is, and a move reads it to tell a re-bind (the target machine is in scope) from a copy (it is not, so a new volume is filled through `data_source`). Each entry a Reference (common-elements §2.5). Absent means the provider did not say, never "anywhere".

relationships.name: provisioned_by
relationships.description: The StorageCluster that provisions this volume (binds its block_storage_class / file_storage_class output). A volume cannot outlive its provisioning cluster.

relationships.name: realizes_disk
relationships.description: Declared on the volume: this volume realizes one named disk of a Machine, joining on the disk name carried in spec.disk_entry (the edge itself carries no qualifier).

relationships.name: restored_from
relationships.description: The snapshot this volume was filled from (spec.data_source names it). Lineage, read at provisioning.

relationships.name: replica_of
relationships.description: The volume this one replicates (spec.replica_of names it). Declared on the replica, so a source never lists its copies.

relationships.name: cloned_from
relationships.description: The volume this one was cloned from (spec.data_source names it). Lineage, read at provisioning.

adopts.role: consumable-volume request vocabulary (capacity, accessModes, volumeMode, storageClass, reclaimPolicy, dataSource) and the CSI accessible-topology semantics behind `accessible_from`
storage-volume-as-asset vocabulary (CapacityBytes, AccessCapabilities) — same family as StorageCluster

context.purpose: Declares a consumable persistent volume — the block or file storage a workload attaches — independent of what provisions it.
context.plain_description: The unit of storage a workload asks for and attaches: requested `capacity`, how concurrently it may be attached — `access_mode`, in the model's snake_case spelling: `read_write_once`, `read_only_many`, `read_write_many`, `read_write_once_pod` (the Kubernetes camelCase forms do not validate) — `volume_mode` (filesystem versus raw block), and which `storage_class` provisions it. It is distinct from the platform that builds it and the devices that back it. Once realized, the provider's volume handle comes back, tying the request to the actual volume.
use_when: You need a workload's storage requested by capacity, access mode, and class, portable across provisioners.
You need volumes ordered in the graph: realized before their consumer, never outliving their provisioning cluster.
not_for: The provisioning policy — StorageClass; the volume references a class by name.
The storage platform — StorageCluster provisions volumes.
Host-local ZFS/LVM storage a host service mounts — Volume.ZFS.
works_with: StorageClass — the class declaring what kind of storage the volume gets.
Machine — the machine whose named disk it realizes (`realizes_disk`).
VolumeSnapshot — a point-in-time copy it can be restored from (`data_source`).
Volume — the volume it replicates (`replica_of`), or the replicas that follow it.
Database — databases whose data directory it backs.
